extracted.intended_audience: students and readers learning algebraic topology / covering space theory (undergraduate/graduate level)
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, criteria, and constructions for group actions that produce covering spaces (condition (*), freeness, proper discontinuity), plus the Cayley complex and graph-based results (maximal trees, fundamental group of a graph, covering spaces of graphs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition (*) (neighborhood-disjointness for covering space actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each y ∈ Y has a neighborhood U such that the images g(U) for varying g ∈ G are pairwise disjoint (equivalently U ∩ g(U) ≠ ∅ implies g is the identity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suffices to take one of the g's to be the identity in the definition. This condition is used to identify actions that yield covering spaces via the quotient Y → Y/G. The text calls an action satisfying (*) a 'covering space action' (not standard terminology).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotient map is a normal covering when (*) holds (Proposition 1.40(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an action of G on Y satisfies (*), then the quotient map p: Y → Y/G (p(y)=Gy) is a normal covering space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reason: for U as in (*), p identifies the disjoint homeomorphic sets {g(U)} to a single open set p(U), and p restricts to a homeomorphism from each g(U) onto p(U). Normality follows since conjugation by group elements permutes the sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deck transformation group equals G when Y is path-connected (Proposition 1.40(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the action satisfies (*) and Y is path-connected, then G is the group of deck transformations of the covering p: Y → Y/G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any deck transformation is determined by its value on a point; for a given y, f(y) lies in the same orbit Gy so equals g(y) for some g ∈ G; uniqueness then implies f=g. Thus the deck group contains G and equals it under path-connectedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algebraic description of G via fundamental groups (Proposition 1.40(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If Y is path-connected and locally path-connected, then G is isomorphic to π1(Y/G)/p_*(π1(Y)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In particular, when Y is simply-connected, π1(Y/G) ≅ G: elements of G correspond to loops in Y/G given by projection of paths from a basepoint y0 to g(y0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Free action (definition and equivalent formulations)
rubrics_metrics.description: An action is free iff it has no fixed points: only the identity element of G fixes any point y ∈ Y. Equivalently, for each y, the images g(y) are all distinct (g1(y)=g2(y) only when g1=g2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Freeness is equivalent to the absence of nontrivial g with g(y)=y. Although (*) implies freeness, freeness alone does not imply (*).

rubrics_metrics.name: Properly discontinuous action (definition and relation to (*))
rubrics_metrics.description: An action is properly discontinuous if every x ∈ X has a neighborhood U such that U ∩ g(U) is nonempty for only finitely many g ∈ G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a weaker condition than (*). Many symmetry groups (e.g., plane tilings) are properly discontinuous but fail (*) because of fixed points. For Hausdorff spaces, freeness plus proper discontinuity implies (*). Proper discontinuity is automatic for finite group actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: (*) implies freeness but not conversely (counterexample)
rubrics_metrics.description: Condition (*) implies the action is free, but a free action need not satisfy (*).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counterexample: Z acting on S^1 by rotation through an irrational multiple of 2π is free (no fixed points) but each orbit is dense, so (*) fails because orbits are not discrete subspaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computing π1 via group actions on simply-connected spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: If G acts on a simply-connected, locally path-connected space Y by a covering space action, then π1(Y/G) is isomorphic to G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under this isomorphism an element g ∈ G corresponds to the homotopy class of the projection of any path in Y from y0 to g(y0); well-defined because Y is simply-connected. This is the method used to compute π1(S^1) from R→S^1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cayley complex / universal cover construction (groups → cell complexes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a group presentation G = ⟨g_α | r_β⟩, construct the 2-complex X_G by wedging circles (one per generator) and attaching 2-cells (one per relator); the universal cover X̃_G (Cayley complex) has a free action of G by left multiplication, and X̃_G is simply-connected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The action is a covering space action whose orbit space is X_G. The fundamental group of X_G is isomorphic to G (via the map sending loop of generator to generator). This provides many examples of covering space actions and of universal covers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of Cayley graph/complex from generators and relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Cayley graph: vertices are group elements g, with an edge from g to g g_α for each generator g_α; each relator r_β determines loops at each vertex and yields attached 2-cells giving the Cayley complex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: G acts on the Cayley complex by left multiplication (g': v ↦ g v), extending to edges and 2-cells. The Cayley complex is connected and simply-connected, so it is the universal cover of the presentation complex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Every covering space of a graph is a graph (Lemma 1A.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a graph and p: X̃ → X is a covering space, then X̃ has a graph structure with vertices p^{-1}(X^0) and edges given by lifts of edges of X; the covering projection is a local homeomorphism of graphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lifts of the attaching maps I → X give the edge structure on X̃; the topology coincides with the weak topology of the graph because the covering projection is a local homeomorphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of maximal trees in connected graphs (Proposition 1A.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every connected graph contains a maximal tree; moreover any tree subgraph is contained in a maximal tree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: inductively adjoin edges to build a subtree containing all vertices; the union deformation retracts to the starting tree. Maximality here means not contained in a larger tree (equivalently contains all vertices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental group of a graph is free with basis from non-tree edges (Proposition 1A.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a connected graph X with maximal tree T, π1(X) is a free group generated by loops f_α determined by each edge e_α of X  ackslash T (go from basepoint along T to one endpoint, cross e_α, return along T).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows because contracting T yields a wedge of circles whose loops correspond to edges outside T. Consequently adjoining any edge to a maximal tree produces nontrivial π1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Every subgroup of a free group is free (Theorem 1A.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a free group F, any subgroup G ≤ F is free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof via topology: realize F as π1(X) for a graph X, then the covering space X̃ corresponding to subgroup G is itself a graph, so π1(X̃) ≅ G is free.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tree characterization and unique nonbacktracking paths
rubrics_metrics.description: A connected graph X is a tree iff it contains no subgraph homeomorphic to a circle; in a tree there is a unique nonbacktracking edgepath joining any two points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One can define a height function on a tree from an inductive maximal-tree construction; downward edges define unique monotone paths to a base vertex. The presence of any nontrivial loop contradicts tree property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graph topology basics (weak topology, local path-connectedness, metric condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A graph has the weak topology with basis open intervals in edges and path-connected neighborhoods of vertices; graphs are locally path-connected. The weak topology is metrizable iff each vertex is the endpoint of only finitely many edges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compact subsets of a graph meet only finitely many vertices and edges; if a vertex has infinitely many incident edges the weak topology is not metric because sequences escaping along distinct edges cannot converge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction to preimage of subspace yields covering (Exercise 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a covering p: X̃→X and a subspace A ⊂ X, the preimage Ã = p^{-1}(A) with restriction p: Ã→A is a covering space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The restriction of a covering to the preimage of a subspace remains a local homeomorphism with discrete fibers over A; used to study coverings of subspaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product of coverings is a covering (Exercise 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If p1: X1→Y1 and p2: X2→Y2 are covering spaces then p1 × p2: X1 × X2 → Y1 × Y2 is a covering space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The product of local homeomorphisms is a local homeomorphism; fiber cardinalities multiply. This lets one build higher-dimensional covers from lower-dimensional ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local path-connectedness necessary for lifting criterion (Exercise 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Local path-connectedness of the domain is a necessary hypothesis for the path/lifting criterion: there exist simply-connected spaces Y and maps f: Y→S^1 that do not lift to the universal cover R→S^1 when Y is not locally path-connected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the quasi-circle Y (subset of R^2 consisting of sin(1/x)-graph plus a segment collapsed to a point) has π1(Y)=0 but f does not lift; thus local path-connectedness cannot be dropped from lifting theorems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Galois correspondence between covering spaces and subgroups (Exercise 24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a covering space X̃→X/G arising from a covering space action of G on X̃, path-connected covering spaces between X̃ and X/G correspond to subgroups H ⊂ G via quotients X̃/H; two such covers X̃/H1 and X̃/H2 are isomorphic iff H1 and H2 are conjugate; X̃/H→X/G is normal iff H is normal, in which case deck group is G/H.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the standard correspondence: subgroups ↔ intermediate covers; normal subgroups ↔ normal (Galois) covers with quotient deck group. Use to classify intermediate coverings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free + properly discontinuous action on Hausdorff space implies covering space action (Exercise 23)
rubrics_metrics.description: If G acts freely and properly discontinuously on a Hausdorff space X then the action satisfies (*) and hence is a covering space action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper discontinuity was defined earlier (each point has neighborhood meeting only finitely many translates). For finite groups on Hausdorff spaces this condition holds automatically, so finite free actions give coverings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Components of covering correspond to orbits and stabilizers correspond to subgroups (Exercise 26)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a covering p: X̃→X with X connected, the components of X̃ correspond bijectively to the orbits of the action of π1(X,x0) on the fiber p^{-1}(x0); under the Galois correspondence the subgroup corresponding to the component containing a given lift x̃0 is the stabilizer of x̃0 (elements leaving x̃0 fixed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This relates the algebraic action of π1 on the fiber to the topology of the covering, and identifies subgroup = stabilizer in the action on the fiber.
